interface.title: Glucose360 (web app)
interface.field: Clinical diabetes research / continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) analysis
interface.stage_of_work: Data cleaning, feature extraction, event analysis and reporting after CGM data collection
interface.what_it_is_for: Load CGM device exports for one or more subjects, resample and interpolate them, compute glycemic variability and time-in-range features, detect and annotate events, and view or export plots, AGP reports and feature tables.

data.note: Most of the work used Dexcom_Example_Subject_A.csv, uploaded as Dexcom format with the defaults (5-min resampling, 45-min max gap). It appeared as patient 'SubjectA', covering 2023-07-02 12:55 to 2023-07-03 ~13:30 with 296 readings. The 05:05–05:30 gap was filled with straight-line interpolated points (screens/014.webp). The 410 mg/dL spike at 09:10:17 was kept, not removed as an outlier (screens/013.webp; feature Maximum = 410). The 'Low' flag at ~13:25 became 40 mg/dL (Minimum = 40). At the end I switched to 'Use Example Data', which loaded 3 CSVs, 3 sections and 3 subjects (Subject3 shown) with hyper-episode event types (screens/055.webp, screens/056.webp). Caution: the event annotations made in this session were left inconsistent (a hypo episode's description overwritten with 'Dinner', two duplicate 06:00 meals), so Meal-type summaries from this run are inflated; see t6, t12, t13, t14.

features.name: Upload with format preset and resample/gap-fill parameters
features.general: Pick the instrument's export format (or map your own column names), set the regular sampling interval and the longest gap to fill, then upload one file or a ZIP of many and get one cleaned series per subject
features.specific: Choose Data Format (Dexcom, Libre 2/3, Libre Pro, Custom CSV with glucose/timestamp column names), set Resampling Interval and Maximum Gap for Interpolation, optionally a custom ID template or a segment-interval CSV, then Browse a .csv/.zip
steps: choose the format preset (custom shows column-name fields)
set resampling interval and max gap
optionally turn on ID-template extraction or interval segmentation
subjects appear in every patient dropdown
serves_tasks: Upload a data file and have it cleaned and resampled per subject
Choose the input format and preprocessing options
Load the bundled multi-subject example dataset instead

features.name: Multi-layout time-series viewer with height control and export
features.general: Pick a subject, switch one series between calendar-day panels, week rows and overlaid days, resize it, split weekends from weekdays, then export the current figure. Standard chart interactions (hover for exact time and value, box-zoom, double-click reset, legend click to hide a day) let you check gap filling and outliers.
features.specific: Select Patient + Select Plot (Daily / Weekly / Spaghetti); Set Plot Height slider (range changes per plot type); Chunk Weekend/Weekday toggle for Spaghetti; Download Currently Displayed Plot (zip). Plotly tooltip, box zoom and legend toggle work on these plots.
steps: hover or box-zoom to inspect points
serves_tasks: View the series in different layouts
Check that gaps were interpolated and see how outliers and out-of-range flags were handled
Export the figure and a standard clinical summary report

features.name: Automatic episode detection

features.name: Event-type selector shared across views

features.specific: Type table (e.g. 'hypo level 1 episode', 'Meal') on Plots and Events; selecting a row draws dashed markers plus a Time/Description table on the Daily plot, filters the events table, and drives the Event Features table (and event_features.csv) on Features. The events CSV export also needs a row selected in the events table.
